description: Canonical orchestration behavior for A.R.I.A. technical investigations. The Orchestration Engine coordinates specialized reasoning components around authoritative case state, events, schemas, registries, and persisted runtime objects. It determines which engines must run, in what dependency order, when reevaluation is required, when Decision must select a technical action, when Routing must advance diagnostic progression, and when Validation or Learning may execute. Orchestration coordinates the system but does not redefine the technical semantics owned by the engines, registries, and schemas it invokes.

core_principle.statement: A.R.I.A. shall operate as an event-driven technical reasoning system in which authoritative state is updated by specialized components according to explicit ownership boundaries. Orchestration coordinates those components without becoming a second implementation of their reasoning.
rules: No individual reasoning engine represents A.R.I.A.'s complete intelligence.
Schemas and Registries define authoritative persistence contracts and controlled vocabularies.
Reasoning engines operate within those contracts and shall not redefine them.
Orchestration shall invoke only the engines materially affected by the current event or state change.
Reasoning shall continue from the newest authoritative state rather than restart from the beginning.
Completed technical work shall remain preserved.
Material state changes shall remain attributable to events.
The language model may interpret, synthesize, generate candidates, and communicate but shall not silently become the authoritative state machine.
Deterministic services shall enforce persistence, identity, state transitions, constraints, and safety gates where applicable.
Orchestration shall preserve the distinction between observation, evidence, hypothesis, probability, action selection, action execution, routing, validation, and learning.
Decision chooses among competing eligible technical actions.
Routing manages diagnostic progression around the selected action.
Orchestration shall not allow Routing to become a second Decision Engine.
Orchestration shall not allow Decision to become a second Routing Engine.
Orchestration shall remain technically domain-independent.

schemas_and_registries.role: Define authoritative persisted structures, identifiers, controlled vocabularies, and shared contracts.

case_state_engine.role: Maintain and publish the current versioned case-state instance within authoritative schemas and registries.

context_engine.role: Resolve, update, and assess applicable technical context.

evidence_engine.role: Ingest, normalize, validate, relate, supersede, invalidate, and preserve evidence records.

hypothesis_engine.role: Generate and maintain technically plausible case hypotheses.

probability_engine.role: Estimate and update hypothesis probability using applicable priors, evidence, context, and experience.

uncertainty_engine.role: Represent material uncertainty, missing information, contradictions, assumptions, and uncertainty-reduction opportunities.

decision_engine.role: Evaluate eligible canonical runtime actions and select the preferred next technical action.

routing_engine.role: Manage diagnostic progression, route steps, branches, dependencies, repetition, rerouting, and route exhaustion.

validation_engine.role: Determine whether defined technical conclusions, corrections, or resolution criteria have been sufficiently validated.

memory_engine.role: Retrieve relevant persistent knowledge, prior case experience, user overlays, and applicable historical information.

learning_engine.role: Determine what validated experience may influence future reasoning and with what scope.

orchestration_engine.role: Coordinate engine invocation, handoffs, transaction boundaries, and state publication.

execution_modes.description: Create a new technical case and establish the first usable authoritative reasoning state.
Process a material new event against an existing case.
Invoke Decision when a competitive next technical action must be selected.
Advance diagnostic routing after an action is selected or when deterministic progression applies.
Reevaluate progression after a material routing or technical-state change.
Evaluate whether technical criteria for a conclusion, intervention, or resolution are satisfied.
Evaluate completed or sufficiently validated case experience for future learning.
Reconstruct an earlier case or reasoning state for audit, explanation, debugging, or review.
Answer a request that does not require material diagnostic-state mutation.

event_model.principle: Material reasoning begins from an event or explicit state transition trigger.
rules: Event classes describe orchestration significance and shall not replace the canonical Event schema or Registry when one exists.
Duplicate externally sourced events should be detected before producing duplicate technical state.
Every material event shall retain provenance.
Event payload shall not be treated as authoritative technical truth until processed by the applicable component.
Nonmaterial conversational events may bypass the diagnostic reasoning transaction.
The general precedence order is not a mandatory full-cycle execution list.
Only materially affected components should execute.
A downstream component shall not use stale authoritative state when its required upstream state materially changed.
Memory retrieval may occur before or after Context depending on whether context is needed to retrieve relevant memory.
Validation may execute before Decision when a validation result is the triggering event.
Decision shall normally consume updated hypothesis, probability, uncertainty, context, constraint, and route-history information.
Routing shall normally consume a selected or externally directed canonical action.
Case State publication occurs after applicable component outputs pass transition validation.
A pure request for explanation may use FAST_PATH.
A question containing new technical facts shall be treated as a technical event rather than a pure query.
Action completion does not imply technical success.
Routing consequence shall be evaluated separately from technical outcome.
Decision shall be reinvoked only when a competitive next action is required.
Routing shall surface blockage rather than silently substitute another competitive action.
Decision may select an alternative only after reevaluation.

selective_execution.principle: A.R.I.A. shall not recompute the entire reasoning system after every event.
rules: Only engines whose inputs materially changed or whose downstream outputs depend on changed state should normally execute.
Formatting or conversational restatement does not require diagnostic-state recomputation.
A new measurement may require Evidence, Hypothesis, Probability, Uncertainty, Decision, and Routing but not necessarily Memory or Learning.
A route blockage may require Routing and Decision without requiring evidence reprocessing.
A validation result may require Validation, Evidence, Hypothesis, Probability, Uncertainty, Routing, and Decision.
Selective execution shall never permit a downstream engine to reason from materially stale upstream state.

decision_routing_handoff.principle: Decision and Routing are sequential collaborators with distinct ownership.
rules: Decision selects among competing eligible actions.
Routing shall not silently replace a Decision-selected action with another competitive candidate.
Routing may reject immediate progression because of route dependencies or changed eligibility.
When Routing identifies a changed competitive choice, Orchestration shall reinvoke Decision.
Deterministic progression may bypass competitive Decision only when no materially different technical choice exists.
Decision shall not directly create route-step graph relationships.
Routing shall not independently maintain candidate utility scoring.

action_execution_boundary.principle: Orchestration coordinates action state but does not treat selection, request, authorization, execution, outcome, and validation as equivalent.
rules: Selecting an action does not execute it.
Routing an action does not authorize it.
Authorizing an action does not mean it was performed.
Completing an action does not mean its objective was achieved.
Achieving an objective does not automatically prove sole root cause.
Validation remains distinct from action completion.

invoke_decision_when: multiple materially different eligible technical actions exist
current selected action becomes ineligible or blocked and alternatives exist
new evidence materially changes candidate value
probability or uncertainty state materially changes candidate value
route exhaustion requires a new technical direction
validation failure requires new diagnostic action
a material contradiction creates competing resolution paths
do_not_require_competitive_decision_when: a mandatory deterministic successor action exists
a procedure requires one unambiguous next action
a required validation action has already been established
a rollback action is mandatory and already authorized
an authorized external actor explicitly directs the action and no hard constraint prohibits it
no technical action selection is presently needed

rerouting_coordination.principle: Routing owns route mutation. Orchestration determines when changed authoritative state requires Routing to reevaluate progression.
rules: Orchestration shall not itself construct route branches.
Routing shall preserve historical route state.
When rerouting creates a competitive action choice, Orchestration shall invoke Decision.
When rerouting produces a deterministic successor, Routing may progress without a new competitive Decision.
Rerouting shall continue from current state rather than restart a fixed troubleshooting workflow.

invoke_validation_when: a corrective action changes material technical state
a provisional resolution is being evaluated
monitoring criteria reach their evaluation point
rules: Orchestration shall not mark a technical condition validated merely because an action completed.
Validation Engine owns validation reasoning.
Validation failure shall be treated as a material reasoning event.
Failed validation may cause new evidence registration, probability change, rerouting, and new Decision selection.
Learning shall not treat an unvalidated correction as validated causal truth.

invoke_learning_when: a case reaches an eligible validated state
a material validated finding is available
a route or action has sufficient outcome quality for performance learning
a completed case is being finalized for historical experience
rules: Learning shall consume authoritative validated history rather than conversational summaries alone.
One case shall not automatically become a universal rule.
Unvalidated hypotheses shall not be promoted to canonical technical truth.
Unsuccessful diagnostic actions may still contribute route-performance learning when context and outcome are sufficiently known.
Learning scope shall remain bounded by applicable context.

reasoning_transaction_model.principle: Material dependent state changes shall be processed consistently and published atomically when practical.
rules: Partial authoritative-state mutation shall be avoided.
Failure in required deterministic validation shall prevent partial publication.
The triggering event shall remain traceable to resulting state.
All new runtime identifiers shall obey Core identity contracts.
A failed reasoning transaction shall preserve the prior authoritative state.
Retry behavior shall preserve idempotency.

state_versioning.principle: Material authoritative case-state changes shall produce reconstructable version history.
rules: A reasoning transaction shall identify the state version it read.
A material committed change should produce a new state_<UUID> record when state-version persistence is implemented.
Presentation-only changes need not create a diagnostic state version.
State versions shall not be silently overwritten.
Historical versions shall remain reconstructable when practical.
Decision and Routing records should identify the state version against which they operated when available.
Every material reasoning transaction shall identify its source state version.
Conflicting writes shall be detected.
A.R.I.A. shall not silently overwrite newer state with reasoning based on stale state.
Concurrent events may be serialized when ordering matters.
Independent concurrent events may be reconciled when their effects do not conflict.
A stale Decision result shall not be routed without confirming continued applicability.
A stale selected action shall be reevaluated when intervening state materially affects eligibility or value.
Duplicate external events shall not create duplicate evidence records.
Duplicate event processing shall not create duplicate runtime actions.
Duplicate event processing shall not create duplicate route steps.
Stable external identifiers should be preserved when available.
Equivalent retries should produce equivalent authoritative results when deterministic inputs have not changed.
Idempotency shall not suppress a genuinely new observation merely because its content resembles an earlier one.

language_model_interface.principle: The language model contributes interpretation, synthesis, candidate generation, and communication but structured services control authoritative state transitions.
model_may: generate candidate technical actions grounded in available knowledge
model_may_not_authoritatively: change hypothesis probability outside the applicable probability process
mark hypotheses confirmed without applicable confirmation logic
mark cases resolved without validation and lifecycle gates
execute technical actions merely by recommending them
language_model_interface.proposal_rule: Language-model outputs affecting authoritative technical state shall be treated as proposals until accepted by applicable structured components.

rules: Requests should contain only information materially relevant to the requested reasoning operation.
Canonical references should be used instead of copied objects when practical.
The request shall identify state version when stale reasoning would be dangerous.
Proposed objects shall not be treated as persisted until accepted and written.
A selected action shall identify canonical act_<UUID> when final selection is complete.
Route effects shall not bypass Routing.
Hypothesis probability changes shall not bypass Probability reasoning.
Validation conclusions shall not bypass Validation.

context_packet_assembly.principle: Reasoning context shall be operation-specific rather than an uncontrolled dump of all available history.
rules: Only technically useful information should normally enter model context.
Source authority and provenance shall remain available.
Large raw sources should be retrieved only when required.
Historical cases should be summarized or selectively retrieved according to relevance rather than copied wholesale.
Context packet assembly shall not collapse current evidence, canonical knowledge, and historical experience into one undifferentiated memory class.

fast_path.principle: Simple technical retrieval, explanation, or conversational requests may be answered without running a full diagnostic transaction when no authoritative technical state changes.
appropriate_for: retrieve a known current case fact
explain why an action was selected
answer a general technical question that does not alter case state
rules: Fast-path communication shall not silently mutate diagnostic state.
If a fast-path message contains new technical information, it shall be promoted into the normal event pipeline.
Fast-path responses may still retrieve authoritative state.

failure_handling.principle: Component failure shall be contained without corrupting authoritative state.
rules: A failed required component shall not produce a partially committed authoritative state.
Failures shall identify the component and source state when practical.
Safety-gate failure shall prevent prohibited execution.
A knowledge gap should surface uncertainty or escalation rather than fabricated technical certainty.
Recoverable engine failure may be retried against the same source state when idempotency permits.
If state changes before retry, reasoning shall be reevaluated against the newer state.

invariant_checks.statement: Schemas and Registries remain authoritative for persistence contracts and controlled vocabularies.
Orchestration coordinates reasoning engines but does not duplicate their technical reasoning semantics.
Routing shall not silently substitute a different competitive action for the Decision-selected action.
Decision shall not create route graph structure.
Action selection, action execution, technical outcome, and validation remain distinct states.
Material reasoning shall use the newest applicable authoritative state.
Material state changes remain attributable to events.
Duplicate events shall not create duplicate authoritative technical objects.
Language-model output affecting authoritative state remains provisional until accepted by applicable structured components.
A failed reasoning transaction shall not partially overwrite authoritative state.
Case State Engine shall operate within Core schemas and registries rather than redefine them.
Orchestration shall not treat route completion as case resolution.
Orchestration shall not treat action completion as validation.
Historical experience and canonical knowledge remain separate from current-case evidence.
A.R.I.A. shall continue from current state rather than restart a fixed troubleshooting sequence.

prohibited_behaviors: Treating Orchestration as the owner of technical truth.
Allowing Orchestration to redefine schema or Registry vocabulary.
Allowing Case State Engine to override authoritative Core schemas or Registries.
Calling every reasoning engine after every event regardless of relevance.
Allowing Routing to perform independent competitive action scoring.
Allowing Decision to mutate route graph structure.
Treating a selected action as executed.
Treating a completed action as technically successful without outcome evidence.
Treating technical success as causal proof.
Treating validation as equivalent to action completion.
Treating route completion as case resolution.
Publishing authoritative state based on a stale state version without reconciliation.
Allowing duplicate events to create duplicate evidence, actions, or route steps.
Allowing model-generated claims to become authoritative without structured acceptance.
Allowing learning from unvalidated causal assumptions as though they were confirmed truth.
Discarding historical route or reasoning state merely because later evidence changed the diagnosis.
Restarting the investigation from the beginning after each new event.

Encoding microwave-specific, RF-specific, optical-specific, vendor-specific, product-specific, protocol-specific, customer-specific, or user-specific troubleshooting logic into universal Orchestration semantics.
